title: Keep configuration and session artifacts out of download operations
description:
Fork research: parallel GPT-6 Astra source reviews, 2026-10-25. Current application baseline: 3ae404b.

## Purpose and evidence

Security prerequisite identified while evaluating fork session caches. Closed #70 hides cloud-torrent.json in listFiles only. The direct download handler opens any confined path, and ZIP creation walks regular files without the same exclusion. Thus UI hiding does not enforce a control-file boundary. Session persistence must not introduce downloadable magnets, private tracker credentials or operational state. This finding is from source inspection, not a live exploit test.

## Acceptance criteria

- Keep new session/control state in an operator-controlled private directory outside served downloads; reject unsafe overlap or provide a documented safe migration.
- Enforce protection of the actual configured config path and operational-state locations for direct GET/HEAD, folder ZIP, DELETE and recursive parent deletion, including paths/aliases that refer to the same protected objects. Filename filtering alone is insufficient.
- Keep private artifacts out of listings and aggregate displayed sizes. Preserve legitimate ordinary downloads, confinement and existing active-file deletion protections.
- Cover nested/renamed config paths, direct URL access despite hidden listing, archives, alias/link cases, recursive deletion and normal file/range/ZIP retrieval using isolated fixtures.

## Sources

- https://github.com/jpillora/cloud-torrent/blob/3ae404b282d7678f90e16b0bf84a52d872fc73d9/server/files.go
- https://github.com/jpillora/cloud-torrent/blob/3ae404b282d7678f90e16b0bf84a52d872fc73d9/server/server.go
- https://github.com/boypt/simple-torrent/blob/6f4942933b71106bae00b4f4c94438e3b315fca2/engine/engineCache.go#L21-L55

## Scope

Implement within the existing Go engine, typed API, generated frontend models and authenticated handler chain. Use isolated legal fixtures; never test against live downloads. This is a new backlog item, not a claim that the proposed behavior already exists.
